**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding Corio:

- **§2.7 "Restrictions"** is a standard IP-protective license restriction (no copying, reverse engineering, or access outside the Agreement) — it constrains use of Commerce One's Software, not our business.
- **"Territory" (§1.11, North America)** and **"Corio Market Segment" (§1.3, customers under $1B)** define the *scope of the license granted to us*, not covenants against competing. §2.10 additionally obliges Commerce One not to unreasonably withhold worldwide expansion at no extra cost.
- **§13.6** affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently, plus a mutual covenant not to sue.
- **§11.3** carries no surviving post-term restriction on our activities.

Targeted searches for "compete/competing", "exclusive", "shall not", "may not", "solicit" and "restrict" returned nothing restricting the businesses we may run or the products we may buy or build. This meets the playbook's preferred position, so nothing to negotiate here.
